anomalies.observed: The reference designator R27 is used twice on the board for two different, unrelated components with conflicting values: on the 'Motion Sensing' sheet R27 is a 50k 0.1% resistor in the VMOT->VMEAS voltage divider (alongside R53/R54/R55), while on the 'LED Enable and E-Stop Config' sheet R27 is a 130R series resistor for the LED_RED indicator D8 hanging off the ESTOP_SINK_ALL node.
anomalies.expected: Every physical component must carry a unique reference designator so the BOM, netlist and silkscreen agree; a single ref like R27 cannot denote both a 50k precision divider resistor and a 130R LED current-limit resistor.

evidence.quote: Motion Sensing sheet: '50k 0.1% R27' in the R53/R54/R27/R55 divider from VMOT to VMEAS/GND
LED Enable and E-Stop Config sheet: '130R R27' in series with LED_RED D8 on the ESTOP_SINK_ALL node

anomalies.impact: Duplicate/conflicting designator corrupts the BOM and silkscreen: an assembler sourcing 'R27' from the BOM may populate the wrong footprint (e.g. a 130R LED resistor dropped into the high-impedance ADC divider, or a 50k resistor in the LED path), breaking input-voltage sensing accuracy or the e-stop indicator, and the two nets share a ref so any correction to one silently mislabels the other.
